skill: Translate a linear system with naturally ordered non-x,y,z variables into its coefficient or augmented matrix; easy instances directly read two already ordered equations in two variables.
learner_operation: Read each equation in order; associate each coefficient with the variable's natural column order, including implicit signed units and missing zeros; place the right-hand constant in the final column only for augmented matrices; distinguish the corresponding matrix from five radio choices.
reasoning_steps: Identify variable order (alphabetical or numerical subscript).
At easy difficulty, read the already organized left coefficients and right constants without solving or row reduction.
Preserve equation order as rows and variable order as columns.
For augmented targets append constants; for coefficient targets omit them; match the complete matrix to one radio option.
invariants: Linear systems only; no solving, row reduction, determinants or solution classification.
Easy source questions have two equations, two variables, integer entries and are already organized.
Single correct radio selection among five complete matrix choices.
Worked explanation identifies coefficient matrix and, for augmented targets, constant column.
permitted_variations: Change signed integer coefficients and constants independently, including implicit units and permissible zeros while keeping variables well defined.
Change the ordered variable pair among supported nonstandard letter and indexed-x names.
Permute correct answer position and vary plausible matrix-reading errors.
Change which equation/variable has a negative or unit coefficient: the source sign patterns and repeated constants are incidental.
Coefficient versus augmented target is supported overall, with workload and target evidence respected; an easy-only augmented family is defensible from the easy examples.
For moderate/hard source profiles retain their observed term rearrangements, missing variables, fractions and shapes, with dependent keys and solutions recomputed.
